THE DAILY METALS PULSE | NOVEMBER 20 — WEEKLY CLOSE

#Uranium #Silver #Gold #Copper

☢️ Spot uranium held near $90/lb this week. By Friday’s U.S. close, the Sprott Uranium Miners ETF ($URNM) had lost roughly 15% in five sessions. During that same week, Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power invited bids for about 13.2 million lb of uranium concentrate for delivery from 2028 through 2037. Bids are due December 28.

🇺🇸 Friday brought the inflation reading I was watching this morning. U.S. households now expect 3.7% inflation over the next year, down a full percentage point from October. Fed Governor Lisa Cook still made the case for higher rates. The Nasdaq fell more than 5% as tech selling intensified after Reuters reported that the SEC was examining Nvidia’s accounting practices.

🥇 Gold was bid near $3,525/oz around 4 p.m. New York time, down roughly 9% from last Friday. 🥈 Silver fell from $48.77 to $40.85 over the same stretch. That’s a 16% loss in a week.

🔶 December copper traded near $5.50/lb on Friday, down from $6.09 a week earlier. Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks rose by 3,204 tonnes to 30,846 tonnes. Even after that increase, those warehouses held less than one day’s worth of Chinese copper consumption.

I remain bullish on uranium. What this week sharpened for me is the financing risk. A developer whose shares fall 15% has to issue nearly 18% more shares to raise the same cash. With utilities already seeking supply through 2037, I’m watching which developers can secure a contract a lender will back and get their mines built in time to deliver.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the daily metals pulse.
